Dover.why: SWEP brazed-plate heat exchangers go into CDUs and chillers for data-center liquid cooling, and its connectors serve liquid-cooled racks; AI data-center cooling demand drives record heat-exchanger sales and a capacity doubling
Dover.evidence: Dover Q2 FY2026 (07-23-2026): CEO - 'Through SWEP, we participate across multiple parts of the liquid cooling ecosystem, supplying brazed plate heat exchangers in both coolant distribution unit and chiller OEMs'

players.product: SWEP brazed-plate heat exchangers for coolant distribution unit and chiller OEMs, plus liquid-cooling connectors and OPW couplers / cryogenic cooling infrastructure for data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue grew 7%, or 5% organically, with all five segments growing organically; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 80 basis points to 25.9%; adjusted EPS $2.74, up 12% (CEO).

CEO: heat exchangers delivered their best quarter ever, with particularly strong demand tied to liquid cooling for data centers; Dover is actively working to double capacity for these products over the next 12 months, coming on sequentially over 2H 2026 into 2027; Q2 growth would have been higher with that capacity. In heat exchangers customers are trying to secure supply, a reflection of demand outstripping supply capacity in the market; customers continued placing brazed plate heat exchanger orders further into the future.

CEO: the shift to liquid cooling directly benefits Dover's connector and heat exchanger businesses; through SWEP it supplies brazed plate heat exchangers to both coolant distribution unit and chiller OEMs; OPW supplies couplers, adapters, cryogenic cooling infrastructure and fiberglass trench systems increasingly specified for data center applications by hyperscalers; demand tied to data center infrastructure remains exceptional, with customers securing capacity well ahead of need. CEO: 'we're not a data center play'.

CEO: heat exchanger margins are now expanding because revenue is accelerating in excess of the capital being deployed, after two and a half years of adding capacity ahead of demand; SWEP is Dover's most automated business, so the ramp carries less risk than refrigeration.
Orders increased 16% year-over-year with book-to-bill at 1.06; trailing 12-month bookings up 15% with book-to-bill well above one across all five segments (CEO).

Dover raised its full-year organic growth and adjusted EPS guidance and is committed to double-digit adjusted EPS growth; CFO: full-year CapEx estimate remains $190 million-$210 million and free cash flow guidance 14%-16% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: CapEx $190 million-$210 million; FCF 14%-16% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: secular growth markets (aerospace and defense, steam and gas turbine components and power generation, single-use biopharma, CO2 refrigeration, data center liquid cooling) are approximately 25% of 2026 revenue, up from 20%; turbine and compressor OEM lead times now extend for years; space revenue expected at $50 million this year; a refrigeration facility consolidation shortfall cost about a point to a point and a half of organic growth in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 25% of revenue; $50 million space revenue
